tasks.gr11-drama-poetry-comparison-t3: Topic: Drama study and poetry comparison for Grade 11 English HL. Cover prescribed drama, stagecraft, dramatic irony, soliloquy, motif, tone, and formal poetry comparison. Ask learners to explain the function of specific stagecraft elements, identify dramatic irony in an extract, compare the tone of two poems using textual evidence, describe how a motif develops across a text, and write a thesis statement for a comparative literature response.
tasks.gr11-literary-transactional-responses-t3: Topic: Literary essay writing and transactional responses for Grade 11 English HL. Cover the structure of a literary essay, review writing, formal interview transcripts, and reports. Ask learners to identify the components of a well-structured literary essay, explain the difference between a review and a summary, write a review paragraph with criteria and evidence, use the correct register for a formal report, and evaluate the effectiveness of a prepared oral response.
tasks.gr11-language-consolidation-editing-t3: Topic: Language consolidation and editing for Grade 11 English HL. Cover editing for accuracy, active and passive voice, direct and indirect speech, oral delivery, and exam-style language tasks. Ask learners to convert sentences between active and passive voice, change direct speech to indirect speech, identify and correct language errors in a passage, explain the function of a relative clause, and describe the qualities of an effective prepared oral presentation.
tasks.gr11-meetings-procedures-t3: Topic: Meetings and meeting procedures (Grade 11 English HL, Term 3 oral). Cover the roles of chairperson, secretary and members, quorum, the agenda, motions, seconding and voting, and minutes. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
tasks.gr11-storytelling-praise-poems-t3: Topic: Storytelling and praise poems (Grade 11 English HL, Term 3 oral). Cover shaping a story for listeners, voice and body, and the features of a praise poem (praise names, repetition, exaggeration, imagery, history) and preparing a performance. Describe features only; do not quote existing praise poems or copyrighted texts. Ask questions directly to 'you'.
